Hi Clara / Devon —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our conversation, attached is a draft token profile export we generated from the sample dataset you shared (finworks_token_profile.csv) and a recommended model shortlist (onboarding_model_shortlist.pdf).

High-level asks we want to align on before the technical handoff:
- Confirm peak QPS/expected concurrency and whether the PDFs will be used in-line (affects context length).
- Clarify the fraction of requests that are "single-turn extraction" vs. "multi-turn conversation" (we used 70/30 split in the draft).
- Verify retention/latency SLOs for the pilot (we assumed 150ms P50 for short responses, 500ms for long responses).

Proposed next step: a short sync Wed to finalize the shortlist and token bands so Grace and Marissa can start the implementation plan. Can you do 11:00–11:30 PT?

Attachment notes: finworks_token_profile.csv — contains hourly token counts across a 7-day sample; onboarding_model_shortlist.pdf — includes recommended model variants and quantization suggestions we think balance cost and quality.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — Wed 11:00 PT works for us. Quick answers inline:

- Peak concurrency: we saw spikes to ~45 concurrent inference calls in the sample day; monthly active users are ~25k with a 3x weekday spike potential. Expect pilot to run 10–14 days with traffic mirroring production patterns.
- PDF usage: about 18% of requests include an attached PDF (financial reports). Those requests tend to be longer and often require 2–3-step extraction flows.
- Request mix: the 70/30 split is close to our telemetry — call it 65% single-turn, 35% multi-turn.
- Latency SLO: production target is P95 under 600ms; pilot can be looser (P95 under 900ms).

We reviewed the shortlist PDF quickly — appreciate the cost-oriented notes. Two clarifications:
1) For the "high-quality" candidate, can you confirm if you recommend a 16k or 32k context for the pilot?
2) For quantized variants: will Redwood support automatic fallback to a full-precision model if we see quality drift?

See you Wednesday.

—Clara
Head of Product
FinWorks

On Wed, Jul 16, 2025 at 08:05 AM Clara Yu <clara.yu@finworks.com> wrote:
> Thanks Ben — Wed 11:00 PT works for us. Quick answers inline:
> 
> - Peak concurrency: we saw spikes to ~45 concurrent inference calls in the sample day; monthly active users are ~25k with a 3x weekday spike potential. Expect pilot to run 10–14 days with traffic mirroring production patterns.
> - PDF usage: about 18% of requests include an attached PDF (financial reports). Those requests tend to be longer and often require 2–3-step extraction flows.
> - Request mix: the 70/30 split is close to our telemetry — call it 65% single-turn, 35% multi-turn.
> - Latency SLO: production target is P95 under 600ms; pilot can be looser (P95 under 900ms).

Thanks for the clarifications — good data. A few immediate implications and recommendations from our infra/modeling side:

1) Context length: for the pilot we recommend a hybrid approach: keep a 16k context baseline for conversational flows and enable a 32k context path only for PDF-heavy extraction routes (route-based model selection). That minimizes cost while covering the long-document cases you described.

2) Model shortlist rationale (summary from the attached PDF):
   - Candidate A: Redwood-Open-13B-16k (best quality/latency balance for multi-step extraction)
   - Candidate B: Redwood-7B-q4f32 (cost-efficient, good for single-turn classification/extraction)
   - Candidate C: Redwood-13B-32k-quant (for document-heavy flows when you need extended context)

3) Fallbacks: Redwood platform can automatically route to a full-precision variant on detected quality regressions or if the quantized model falls below a configured metric. We will include a canary and automatic fallback policy in the rollout config.

4) Sizing estimate (pilot window, 14 days): using your sample profile (peak concurrency 45, 65/35 split, 18% PDF):
   - Expected total tokens/day (median estimate): ~42M tokens/day
   - Billed token mix: ~70% generation/30% prompt for the multi-turn cases we measured
   - GPU footprint (steady-state during peak): 6-8 p3-equivalent GPUs for the hybrid routing mix; burst capacity to 12 GPUs for peak windows.

Action items before the handoff:
- Grace: can you produce a short configuration draft (routes + rollout policy + metric-based fallback) based on the above?
- Marissa: please begin a pilot runbook draft with checkpoints at day 3, 7, and 14 to evaluate cost and quality.
- Clara/Devon: please confirm which PDFs we should run through the extended-context path during pilot (a sample list is sufficient).

I can take the config draft and put it into the Console workspace once Grace posts it.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick status update and deliverables: 

- Config draft: attached to the Drive link (route-config-v1.yaml) — includes two routes: /api/extract -> 32k quant path (Candidate C fallback to Candidate A), /api/summary -> 7B quant path (Candidate B with FP fallback).
- Rollout policy: canary at 5% for 24h, then 25% for 48h, with automatic rollback on a 5-point quality delta measured on the evaluation set (we will upload a small eval set to the shared Drive).
- Runbook draft: Marissa has seeded the runbook with the day 3/7/14 checkpoints and a quick-cost dashboard widget (tokens/day, cost/day, P95 latency).

Marissa — can you attach the eval prompt set and a short instruction for the CS team to run the first 100 PDF extraction samples through the 32k path? Clara, if you can point us to the sample PDFs (or drop a link in the Drive), we'll schedule the pilot kickoff for next Monday.

Notes: Estimated cost range for the 14-day pilot (approx): $9k–$13k depending on the actual PDF extraction ratio; we'll refine after the first 72 hours.

Grace O'Connor
Head of CS Engineering (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
